Presl|publisher=The Plant List|access-date=2011-02-20}} }} '''''Campyloneurum phyllitidis''''', commonly known as the '''long strap fern''', is a species of fern in the family [[Polypodiaceae]].{{cite web|url=http://florida.plantatlas.usf.edu/Plant.aspx?id=3649|title=Atlas of Florida Vascular Plants - ''Campyloneurum phyllitidis''|author1=Wunderlin, R. P. |author2=B. F. Hansen|year=2008|publisher=Institute for Systematic Botany, University of South Florida, Tampa.|access-date=2010-02-20}} ==Distribution== ''Campyloneurum phyllitidis'' is found in North, Central, and South America: from [[Florida]], the [[Caribbean]], and southeastern Mexico in the north; to tropical [[Peru]] and [[Brazil]], and [[Paraguay]] in the south. Other countries it is native to include the [[Southeastern United States]], [[Cuba]], [[Costa Rica]], Bolivia, and [[Venezuela]]. It is also present in Florida, Puerto Rico, Hawaii and the Virgin Islands.{{cite web|url=https://plants.usda.gov/java/profile?symbol=CAPH5|title=''Campyloneurum phyllitidis'' (L.) C. Presl|publisher=USDA Plants|access-date=2010-02-20}} The fern is common on [[Barro Colorado Island]] of Panama. ==Description== ''Campyloneurum phyllitidis'' is an [[epiphytic|epiphyte]], growing on other plants; generally the fern is found growing in the canopies of trees. It has a relatively large [[rhizome]] from which many fine [[rootlet]]s covered in dark reddish-brown scales grow. Its leaves are simple in shape, hairless, {{convert|45|-|100|cm|in}} long and {{convert|8|-|12|cm|in}} wide. The [[Sorus|sori]] are round and small, occurring in on both sides of lateral veins of the leaves.{{cite book|author=Thomas B. Croat|title=Flora of Barro Colorado Island|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Whc_ahfhFFoC&pg=PA103|access-date=20 February 2011|year=1978|publisher=Stanford University Press|isbn=978-0-8047-0950-7|pages=103–}} It is known to grow as an epiphyte on ''[[Platypodium elegans]]'', ''[[Ceiba pentandra]]'', ''[[Tabebuia]] guayacan'', ''[[Anacardium excelsum]]'',{{cite journal | doi = 10.1111/j.1744-7429.1997.tb00427.x|author1=Jose Luis Andrade |author2=Park S. Nobel | year = 1997 | title = Microhabitats and Water Relations of Epiphytic Cacti and Ferns in a Lowland Neotropical Forest | journal = Biotropica | volume = 29 | issue = 3 | pages = 261–270 | jstor = 2389141 |bibcode=1997Biotr..29..261A }} ''[[Socratea exorrhiza]]'', ''[[Marila]] laxiflora'' and ''[[Perebea]] xanthochyma''.{{Cite journal | last1 = Laube | first1 = S. | last2 = Zotz | first2 = G. | title = Neither Host-specific nor Random: Vascular Epiphytes on Three Tree Species in a Panamanian Lowland Forest | doi = 10.1093/aob/mcl067 | journal = Annals of Botany | volume = 97 | issue = 6 | pages = 1103–14 | year = 2006 | pmid = 16574691| pmc =2803392 }} ==Uses== ''Campyloneurum phyllitidis'' is cultivated as an [[ornamental plant]], and is the most common species of ''Campyloneurum'' found in cultivation. The fern grows well in well-drained soil under medium levels of light. It needs to be protected from slugs and snails.{{cite book|author1=Barbara Joe Hoshizaki|author2=Robbin Craig Moran|title=Fern grower's manual|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Wq_-jexfHCcC&pg=PA231|access-date=20 February 2011|year=2001|publisher=Timber Press|isbn=978-0-88192-495-4|pages=231–}} ''Campyloneurum phyllitidis'' was grown in England during the Victorian era, when ferns were particularly popular (the phenomenon known as [[pteridomania]]). The fern was described by an author of the time, Shirley Hibberd, as being "very distinct" and that it formed a "striking object when grown well".{{cite book|author=Shirley Hibberd|title=The fern garden: how to make, keep, and enjoy it; or, Fern culture made easy|url=https://archive.org/details/ferngardenhowto01hibbgoog|access-date=20 February 2011|year=1869|publisher=Groombridge and Sons|pages=[https://archive.org/details/ferngardenhowto01hibbgoog/page/n146 107]–}} [[File:Campyloneurum phyllitidis 001.jpg|thumb|left|upright|270px|Close up of ''Campyloneurum phyllitidis'' leaves, with [[Sorus|sori]] on their underside.]] ==See also== * {{C|Pteridophyta of the Americas|Pteridophyta (ferns) of the Americas}} ==References== {{Reflist|25em}} ==External links== *[http://plants.usda.gov/plant-profile?symbol=caph5 USDA Plants Profile for ''Campyloneurum phyllitidis'' (long strapfern)] {{Taxonbar|from=Q5028759}} [[Category:Campyloneurum|phyllitidis]] [[Category:Ferns of the Americas]] [[Category:Flora of the Caribbean]] [[Category:Ferns of Mexico]] [[Category:Ferns of the United States]] [[Category:Flora of Central America]] [[Category:Flora of northern South America]] [[Category:Flora of western South America]] [[Category:Ferns of Brazil]] [[Category:Flora of Florida]] [[Category:Flora of Panama]] [[Category:Epiphytes]] [[Category:Plants described in 1753]] [[Category:Botanical taxa named by Carl Linnaeus]] [[Category:Taxa named by Carl Borivoj Presl]] [[Category:Garden plants of North America]] [[Category:Garden plants of South America]] [[Category:House plants]] [[Category:Flora without expected TNC conservation status]]
